text:
Predicates:
Invertebrate(x) ::: x is an invertebrate.
Vertebrate(x) ::: x is a vertebrate.
Backbone(x) ::: x has a backbone.
ReproduceByMaleAndFemale(x) ::: x reproduces by male-and-female mating.
Bee(x) ::: x is a bee.
Queen(x) ::: x is a queen bee.
Harry ::: Harry.

Premises:
Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates. ::: ∀x (Animal(x) → (Invertebrate(x) ∨ Vertebrate(x))) .
All animals with backbones reproduce by male-and-female mating. ::: ∀x (Backbone(x) ∧ Animal(x) → ReproduceByMaleAndFemale(x)) .
All vertebrate animals have a backbone. ::: ∀x (Animal(x) ∧ Vertebrate(x) → Backbone(x)) .
All bees do not reproduce by male-and-female mating. ::: ∀x (Bee(x) → ¬ReproduceByMaleAndFemale(x)) .
All queen bees are bees. ::: ∀x (Queen(x) → Bee(x)) .
Harry is a bee. ::: Bee(Harry).

Conclusion:
( (Vertebrate(Harry) ∧ Backbone(Harry)) ∨ (¬Vertebrate(Harry) ∧ ¬Backbone(Harry)) ) → (¬Invertebrate(Harry) ∧ ¬Queen(Harry)) ::: If Harry is either both a vertebrate and an animal with a backbone, or neither, then Harry is neither an invertebrate nor a queen bee.
